standard_prerequisites.use: Introduces the object F whose vanishing must be established.

standard_prerequisites.use: Is the structural fact that makes the kernel of multiplication by f detectable.

core_obligations: Denote M_f = M tensor^L_R R_f and choose a distinguished triangle F -> M -> M_f (proof lines 30020-30021).
Use the hypothesis to conclude H^i(M_f) = H^i(M)_f = 0 for i < 0, so that it suffices to show H^i(F) = 0 for i < 0 (proof lines 30021-30022).
Record that H^i(F) is f-power torsion for all integers i (proof line 30023).
Use that f : M_f -> M_f is an isomorphism to conclude that C is isomorphic to the cone of f : F -> F (proof lines 30024-30026).

Conclude by contradiction: if H^i(F) is nonzero then the kernel of f : H^i(F) -> H^i(F) is nonzero, which forces H^{i-1}(C) nonzero; the hypothesis H^i(C) = 0 for i < -1 rules out i - 1 < -1, finishing the argument (proof lines 30027-30029).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an element f, an object M of D(R), and the cone C of the multiplication map f : M -> M; assuming that H^i(M)_f = 0 for i < 0 and that H^i(C) = 0 for i < -1, it concludes that H^i(M) = 0 for i < 0 (source lines 30011-30017). The proof is a triangle argument. It denotes M_f = M tensor^L_R R_f and chooses a distinguished triangle F -> M -> M_f; by hypothesis H^i(M_f) = H^i(M)_f = 0 for i < 0, so it suffices to show that H^i(F) = 0 for i < 0 (proof lines 30020-30022). The proof then records the structural fact that H^i(F) is f-power torsion for every i (proof lines 30023). The substantive observation is that, since f : M_f -> M_f is an isomorphism, C is isomorphic to the cone of f : F -> F, which the proof draws from the octahedral-type statement (proof lines 30024-30026). The conclusion is then a contrapositive: if H^i(F) were nonzero, the kernel of f on H^i(F) would be nonzero, which forces H^{i-1}(C) to be nonzero; the hypothesis H^i(C) = 0 for i < -1 therefore rules out the cases i - 1 < -1, finishing the proof (proof lines 30027-30029). The non-routine content is the identification of C with the self-cone of F, which converts the hypothesis on C into information about the kernel of multiplication by f.
